items.title: A New Class of Buy Now, Pay Later: From Checkout Utility to Enterprise Growth Lever
items.summary: Flexible financing is becoming more than a way to complete a travel purchase. For airlines and other travel brands, the next opportunity is using financing to support brand equity and profits.

items.title: Indian Hotels Company Targets Switzerland and Southeast Asia; Dubai Rebound Stalls
items.summary: IHCL would have preferred to enter Switzerland first, but instead chose Frankfurt, where strong India connectivity promised quicker returns, rather than rushing into a costlier, lower-yield Swiss market.

items.title: Sabre Hackathon Highlights Travel’s Developer Access Divide
items.summary: Hand developers a blank slate on travel's infrastructure, and they don't rebuild search. They go after the phone calls and broken connections travel never digitized — a clear sign on how new or external builders see travel AI's biggest pay-offs.

items.title: Returning to Park Hyatt Tokyo: How a Great Hotel Survives a Renovation
items.summary: Park Hyatt Tokyo proves that preserving a great hotel is less about furniture than judgment. The renovation succeeds. The harder task now is ensuring the next generation of hoteliers can inherit the culture that made the building matter in the first place.

items.title: The Quiet Reinvention of the Hotel Tax
items.summary: The modern American hotel tax was built on one Las Vegas idea from 1955. The argument now is over who controls the money.

items.title: Emirates’ Sir Tim Clark on Retirement: ‘It’s Not Time’
items.summary: Clark insists Emirates is ready for life after him, but his decision to stay on keeps one of aviation’s longest-running succession stories alive.

items.title: The U.S. Passport Is Stuck, The UAE’s Is Gaining Fast
items.summary: Passport rankings are a lagging indicator of something travel companies should watch in real time: how easily — and where — a country's citizens can move.

items.title: Riyadh Air Waited Years for New Planes. Now Six Have Arrived in 30 Days
items.summary: For a startup with no legacy fleet to fall back on, delivery delays were painful. But taking such a large number of aircraft in just a month brings its own headaches.
